decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The hardstanding, by reason of its scale, full coverage of the rear garden, and poor-quality design, results in a development that would result in 'less than substantial' harm to the character and appearance of the Mansfield Conservation area. The works remove the capacity for meaningful soft landscaping and limit the potential for future natural growth within the rear garden. As a result, the proposal is detrimental to the amenity and biodiversity value of the site and the wider area. The development is therefore contrary to Policies A1 (Managing the impact of development), A2 (Open Space), A3 (Biodiversity), D1 (Design) and D2 (Heritage) of the Camden Local Plan 2017.

Reason : 2 - The applicant has failed to provide sufficient supporting information to demonstrate that the hardstanding would incorporate sustainable drainage systems (SUDS) to limit the amount and rate of surface water run-off and waste water entering the combined storm water and sewer network. The proposals are therefore contrary to policy CC3 (Water and flooding) of the London Borough of Camden Local Plan 2017.

Reason : 3 - In the absence of an arboricultural assessment of the rear garden trees, the proposal fails to demonstrate there has not been any detrimental impact on any of the existing trees within the rear garden. As such, the development is contrary to Policies A3 (Biodiversity), D1 (Design), D2 (Heritage), CC2 (Adapting to climate change) and CC3 (Water and flooding) of the Camden Local Plan 2017.

Reason : 4 - The proposal fails to demonstrate that it does not have an adverse impact on local biodiversity. As such, the development is considered contrary to Policies A1 (Amenity), A3 (Biodiversity), D1 (Design), D2 (Heritage), CC2 (Adapting to climate change) and CC3 (Water and flooding) of the Camden Local Plan 2017.
description: Retrospective application for engineering works to rear garden to install hardstanding (sandstone tiles).
